reason: The cited evidence does not involve HfZrTiTa0.53 or any similar refractory high-entropy alloy. E1 describes thermomechanical processing of a different MEA, and E2 discusses a lamellar FCC+B2 eutectic AlCoCrFeNi alloy with L12 precipitation. Neither provides evidence that sub-transus annealing of HfZrTiTa0.53 produces an FCC phase, that such a phase would be ductile, or that strength and impact energy release would be maintained. The key premises are therefore unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Sub-transus annealing of HfZrTiTa0.53 at ~800 °C will induce a dual-phase BCC+FCC microstructure
The FCC phase will be ductile and enhance tensile ductility
Yield strength (~786 MPa) will be maintained after annealing
Impact-triggered energy release will be preserved
Ductile precipitates delay necking and crack initiation via enhanced dislocation mobility
